## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix slug generation for titles with non-ASCII letters or digits, which can produce empty slugs, and add the required verification section to the PR description.

## Changes

The pull request adds a helper that lowercases page titles, replaces runs of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` with hyphens, and trims leading and trailing hyphens. It adds parameterized tests for spaces, repeated hyphens, punctuation-only titles, and empty titles.

## Critical

(none)

## Important

- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Preserve non-ASCII letters and digits — `slugify("東京")` returns an empty string because `[a-z0-9]` excludes both letters and the final strip removes their replacement hyphen. The PR description says the helper replaces non-alphanumeric characters. — Titles written entirely in scripts such as Japanese lose all identifying text in their page URL slugs.
- PR body — correctness — Add the required Testing section — The submitted description explains the slug transformation but omits the verification section required by `AGENTS.md:4`: “Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified.” — Reviewers cannot tell from the description how the change was verified.

## Suggestions

- app/slug.py:7 — tests — Cover digits in page titles — For `Chapter 2`, the regex should retain `2` and return `chapter-2`, but no test exercises the `[0-9]` range. — A regression that drops ASCII digits from page titles would pass the current tests. — Fix: Extend `test_slugify` with `("Chapter 2", "chapter-2")`.
